dataSetInformation.common:generalComment:
An energy saving lamp uses the same principle as a fluorescence or neon (TL) tube. Mercury gas in a partially vacuum tube emits UV light when electrical current is sent trough the tube. A convert on the inside the tube converts the light into the visible spectrum. Energy saving lamps need an adaptor containing the electric swtiches. Energy saving lamps have a much longer life time than normal light bulbs (6-8000 hrs compared to 1000 hrs). Note that when comparing light bulbs with energy saving lamps they should be compared on the basis of the amount of light produced, expressed in lumen. On average a lamp produces aroung 600 lumen. Inventory includes production, production waste, packaging, transport, and waste treatment of the full product.
